claims.text: High-entropy alloys are multicomponent metallic alloys containing multiple principal alloying elements.
The relevant initial states include disordered liquids and high-temperature solids near or above melting.
CoCrFeNiMn-based alloys are representative of the intended multicomponent systems.
The conventional EAM reference should be replaced by a machine-learned interatomic potential trained on diverse ab initio liquid and high-temperature solid configurations.
High-temperature HEA liquids exhibit widespread atomic-configuration fluctuations.
The proposed intervention should apply to canonical quinary or senary HEAs at temperatures near melting.
Training on a wide range of local configurations will enable the potential to capture relevant short-range ordering.
Training on a wide range of local configurations will enable the potential to capture liquid and solid fluctuation effects.
Representative ab initio configurations from both phases will make the machine-learned potential span the target phase space more accurately than an EAM reference.
Improved representation of the target phase space will increase reference-target phase-space overlap.
EAM-based references typically contain non-overlapping phase-space regions that propagate error along thermodynamic-integration paths.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The reduction in free-energy mismatch could amount to tens of percent.
TOR-TILD uses standard EAM potentials as thermodynamic-integration references.
Ab initio sampling is feasible over a sufficiently broad range of high-temperature liquid and solid configurations for the intended HEAs.
The method may not be effective for low-melting or less compositionally complex alloys.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in path mismatch or improvement in phase-space-overlap metrics relative to EAM would falsify the hypothesis.
